title: A Slayer Needs a Watcher
subtitle: The SLAiYER Handbook · Chapter 1 — which AI tool to open for which job, what the words mean, and how to use any of them without getting vamped.
lesson: Which AI tool to open for which job, what the words everyone says actually mean, and how to work with any of them — matching the type to the task, not ranking who's "best."
emotionalBeat: Overwhelm becomes orientation: she stops asking which tool is best and starts matching the type to the task.
oneLineDescription: The one in which "just use AI" finally gets a map — which tool to open for which job, what the words mean, and how to use any of them without getting vamped.
episodeDescription: The one in which the LAiDIES Grimoire opens to its first page, the SLAiYER Handbook, and every AI tool stops being one vague instruction and becomes a type you can place, with a best job and a way to work with it.
previously: She learned that polished AI output still needs receipts: check the claim, the timeline, and the source before it borrows your name.
tryOn: Pick one tool you already have. Take one real task — the email you've been avoiding, the meeting you need summarized. Give it the whole assignment once: who it's for, the goal, the tone, the format. Then read the output like a Watcher, not a believer.
mainCharacterEnergy: "Just use AI" is not an instruction. Match the type to the task.
rememberLine: "Just use AI" is not an instruction. Match the type to the task.
communityPrompt: Which tool did you finally figure out this week, and which one is still tripping you up? Share the situation, not confidential workplace details.
referencesUsed: Romy and Michele's High School Reunion
